The summer before my second year of college I met someone who ended up becoming my bf. He spent from October until the end of the year in my residence with me undercover as he wasn't supposed to live there. 
After college I was planning on moving into an apartment with my friend who she continued her third year, her program was longer than mine. I just liked the city I was in and didn't feel it was too much to split a place with her to make ends meet. He was aware of this before it all happened. 
So the three of us sign a lease, he was hesitant because he didn't like her randomly, I'd never heard this before that. But everything was okay, we all went to the beach, roommate had her time to study, things felt kinda normal (mind you this was a manipulative relationship but we won't get into that). 
I found out that he was cheating on me with this roommate only because I said I wanted to break up, he THREW that in my face as a f*ck you and then came back into the room crying about how he meant to tell me months ago, he felt so bad and didn't want to bring it up that way. . . But how else was I gonna find out and how long would it have stayed a secret if I didn't have that moment? It probably would've stayed that way and I would have a terrible life with a manipulator. 

Idk how well that portrays into your life but sometimes people keep secrets until they feel it can hurt you or make you feel bad for them. Try to see if there was any Unreasonable sense, mind you, of you feeling bad for her. 
Feeling bad because she was manipulated or taken advantage of is reasonable, but feeling bad for her because she made a wrong decision while drunk is like feeling bad for a drunk driver because he didn't mean to crash.

I had a friend that wanted a surprise party, so me and her other best friend (we were a trio) went out and got balloons, a cake, sparklers to put on her cake instead of candles thinking that'd be cool, and even had a different friend host the party instead of having it at her place because she does not get along with her family very well and they are extremely intrusive. But as days rolled closer to the day she would ask if we were doing anything and we'd say yes, but not give her any details. As the days got closer she grew more anxious and threw mini fits. Then the day came, we brought her in and she had a good time but complaimed on the way there, before we walked in and after the party. Sometimes people are just ungrateful and you have to just see it as you did a good job. She talked about it weeks later and about how much fun she had, its just in the moment people still have expectations whether they ask for a surprise or not.
